title: Sequencer simulator test documentation still describes the fixed scripting binding token defect
description: Ticket 8ca68272 (commit 57762ed63) fixed the Scripting Agent change bindings so they forward the local device/master access token. Test documentation still describes that defect as current: indigo_test/integration/sequencer_simulators.md:27 says --native-bindings 'is expected to fail on the current production code'; indigo_test/integration/sequencer_simulators.js:433-434 has a comment about the 'documented native binding-token defect'; indigo_test/integration/run_sequencer_simulators.py:191 has --help text about the same defect. Update these texts to the current behavior. The remaining --native-bindings failure of 'restore private configuration' belongs to ticket 8f313dbc-765b-5e79-9cef-a9d8db5918f9 and is not part of this ticket. Text-only change; no test logic or production code changes.

outcome.summary: Diff is text-only (one markdown line, one JS comment, one argparse help string; git diff --check clean). Verified true: DRIVER_VERSION 0x03000012 = 3.0.0.18 (indigo_agent_scripting.c:28); change_property_handler sets access_token = indigo_get_device_or_master_token() (indigo_agent_scripting.c:392), shared by all three change bindings (lines 413/435/457), and indigo_token.c:111-124 returns the device token, else the master token; relay is still the default (run_sequencer_simulators.py:261 authenticated_relay = not args.native_bindings; sequencer_simulators.js:435-440 replaces exactly the three named bindings); new help text and md describe --native-bindings neutrally and do not claim it passes; test_agent_scripting 'change bindings forward local access tokens' (test_agent_scripting.c:725) exists. No other stale binding-token-defect claim found in indigo_test (excluding shell_compliance/build) or indigo_docs. DEFECT: sequencer_simulators.md:27, rewritten by this change, still states 'the test_protocol_security unset-master regression exposes its separate defect directly. The latter must not be interpreted as fixed by setting a test master token.' That is no longer true on master: b3467d56f (closed ticket 21bfa946, an ancestor of this branch) resolved it as a wrong test expectation; test_protocol_security.c:509-513/538 now asserts that without a master token device tokens have no effect and the write is accepted, as documented in INDIGO_DEVICE_ACCESS_CONTROL_AND_LOCKING.md:21/43. Requested fix: drop or rewrite that clause (e.g. say the unset-master behavior is documented and covered by test_protocol_security 'device ACL requires device or nonzero master token'), keeping it text-only. No tests run (text-only change).

Round 2. The only change since round 1 is commit 6d58f097c, which edits one line, indigo_test/integration/sequencer_simulators.md:27. The full diff against master is still text-only in the same three files (md line, JS comment at sequencer_simulators.js:434, argparse help at run_sequencer_simulators.py:191), and git diff --check is clean. The new ending is true. test_protocol_security.c:509-513/538 asserts that without a master token a device-token-protected write is accepted, which is the behaviour documented in INDIGO_DEVICE_ACCESS_CONTROL_AND_LOCKING.md:21/43. The cited case name matches test_protocol_security.c:554 exactly. Round-1 checks still hold: version 3.0.0.18 = 0x03000012; device-or-master token forwarding at indigo_agent_scripting.c:392 via indigo_token.c:111-124; the relay remains the default (run_sequencer_simulators.py:261); test_agent_scripting.c:725 exists; nothing claims the suite passes with --native-bindings. No stale binding-token-defect text remains in indigo_test (excluding shell_compliance) or indigo_docs. No tests run (text-only change).
